metadata.dataset_name: Ingaze Real-World Messy Client Intake (Discovery Notes + Archetype & Cost Review Surveys + Raw Telemetry)
metadata.usage_note: Unlike the 3 clean benchmark scenarios in ingaze_sandbox_dataset.json (where signals were already summarized), this file mirrors what ACTUALLY arrives when a new B2B client onboards onto Ingaze: rough notes from two initial conversations where stakeholders barely agree on what they want, HR's raw self-reported answers to the Employer Archetype and Recruiting Cost Review intake forms (with bracket estimates and untracked 'N/A' gaps), and raw Outside-In telemetry containing small-sample quirks, out-of-scope review noise, marketing traffic confounders, and unlinked tracking (null). Test your reasoning architecture against this file—Sunday's live test uses this exact messy intake structure! You may also optionally include SCENARIO_REALWORLD_01_VALLEYSYS in your submission.json.

basic_company_facts.industry: B2B Industrial Automation, Packaging Mechatronics & Embedded/Cloud Control Software
basic_company_facts.footprint_and_headcount: ~680 employees total: ~460 across HQ and 2 mechatronic plants in Emilia-Romagna (Modena / Reggio Emilia), ~170 travelling field-commissioning technicians, and ~50 software/IoT engineers in a Milan office opened 2 years ago
basic_company_facts.open_roles_mentioned_verbally: Roughly 35–40 open technical positions this year (C++/PLC Automation & Industrial IoT Software Engineers in Milan/Emilia, plus Specialized Mechatronic & Field Commissioning Technicians)

raw_discovery_call_notes.source: Call 1 — Initial Discovery with Elena (HR Manager) & Marco (Recruiter), 28 min
raw_discovery_call_notes.raw_notes: Elena opened saying hiring engineers has become 'impossible because post-COVID candidates only want 100% remote work from home and US big-tech salaries, and young engineers don't know ValleySys even though we export 85% of our machines worldwide.' She thinks they should shoot a polished 40th-anniversary corporate culture video for the website and double their sponsored job-post budget. Marco (one of only 2 recruiters) chimed in that generalist job boards dump hundreds of unqualified Easy-Apply CVs into their shared mailbox every week—forklift drivers, helpdesk juniors, web designers—so they spend half their week just opening PDFs. Marco also mentioned quietly that for the Milan software hub, 'even when headhunters bring us strong developers, 3 of the last 8 hires resigned before finishing their 6-month probation, and last month 5 shortlisted candidates withdrew while waiting over three weeks for our technical leads to give us calendar slots for the second interview.'

raw_discovery_call_notes.source: Call 2 — Brief Check-in with Ing. Ferretti (Managing Director) & Ing. Riva (Head of Control Software & R&D), 22 min
raw_discovery_call_notes.raw_notes: Ing. Ferretti is frustrated by how much money went to external headhunters over the past year ('over €130k in agency invoices and some of those people didn't even stay till Christmas') and has zero patience for 'HR fluff videos'. He also drew a hard line on LinkedIn: 'Do NOT propose turning our senior engineers into LinkedIn influencers or public brand ambassadors—German machinery competitors and IT consultancies already message our people every week to poach them, I refuse to put our best names in a shop window.' Ing. Riva complained that HR copied trendy startup buzzwords into the software job ads ('Cloud-Native AI, greenfield microservices, flexible smart working'), so candidates arrive at the technical round expecting remote cloud R&D, 'and when I tell them honestly that 70% of year one is on-site C++ and PLC real-time machine integration 5 days a week at the test bench, they decline the offer or quit in month four.' Riva admitted his 4 squad leads in Milan/R&D were promoted straight from senior firmware roles last year because they wrote great code, 'nobody ever taught them how to onboard juniors or run 1-on-1s, they just expect newcomers to figure out 15-year-old repositories alone.' On the Emilia plant & field-commissioning side, Ferretti noted veteran technicians rarely leave, receive a €2,400 annual production bonus plus punctual travel allowances, and bring in most good hires by word of mouth from regional technical institutes—though younger field techs grumble when Monday international installation trips are reassigned on Friday afternoon.

raw_discovery_call_notes.source: Forwarded Internal Email — Giulia (B2B Trade-Fair Marketing), 4 lines
raw_discovery_call_notes.raw_notes: 'Hi Elena, quick heads-up on website numbers: between Oct 8 and Oct 26 we spent €1,800 boosting Instagram/Facebook reels for our Parma Packaging Automation Expo booth and put the Careers page link as secondary CTA. It generated ~6,700 smartphone clicks mostly from trade-fair visitors and university students scrolling on the train who closed the tab right away—nothing to do with your open roles!'

employer_archetype_survey_response.q1_selected_company_archetype: Established Engineering & Export Leader (40-Year Industrial Heritage)
employer_archetype_survey_response.q2_biggest_perceived_obstacle: Candidates don't recognize our brand name, or they get put off by a few harsh online reviews before speaking with us
employer_archetype_survey_response.q3_primary_12_month_goal: Fill technical roles faster without relying on expensive headhunters
employer_archetype_survey_response.q4_internal_budget_approver: Managing Director (strictly cost-and-output driven; skeptical of branding agencies)
employer_archetype_survey_response.q5_current_communication_difficulty: We publish trade-fair stands, client installations, and ISO awards on LinkedIn, but prospective hires never engage
employer_archetype_survey_response.q6_what_we_envy_in_competitors: Software consultancies look modern and appealing to young engineers even though we build real industrial hardware+software
employer_archetype_survey_response.q7_reputation_frustration: Our online score doesn't reflect how financially solid, punctual, and technically advanced the company really is
employer_archetype_survey_response.q8_initiative_hr_believes_they_need: A 40th-anniversary employer branding video + increased sponsored job-board advertising
employer_archetype_survey_response.q9_preferred_hiring_channel: Direct qualified website applications and internal technician referrals
employer_archetype_survey_response.q10_main_retention_concern: Early resignations during the first 6 months in the software/automation team
employer_archetype_survey_response.q12_annual_turnover_rate_reported: N/A (Payroll reports ~10.4% total exits including retirements; HR does not separate voluntary first-year churn by site)

recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.completed_by: Elena (HR Manager) — rapid bracket selection + notes
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q1_rough_exact_hires_note: 38 hires closed in the past 12 months (including replacements); 14 technical roles currently open >60 days
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q3_team_note: 2 recruiters + HR Manager splitting time across admin, union relations, and training
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q4_screening_note: ~16 hours/week per recruiter manually opening PDF CVs in shared inbox; >85% lack C++/PLC or mechatronic qualifications
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q5_process_note: HR phone screen -> HR interview -> Tech Lead round -> Head of R&D round -> GM final sign-off (avg 23 days idle gap between HR and 1st tech round)
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q7_average_time_to_fill_bracket: 2 - 3 months (Over 3 months for Milan software roles)
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q7_rough_days_note: ~64 calendar days overall; ~84 days on software/automation roles
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q8_agency_note: 14 of 38 hires (~36.8%) closed through external headhunters
recruiting_cost_review_survey_response.q9_salary_and_fee_note: ~18% average fee on ~€43,500 gross base salary; agency guarantee expires at 90 days

internal_climate_and_candidate_feedback_.note: No company-wide climate survey exists yet (plant staff dislike long digital questionnaires). HR shared 7 raw exit/candidate notes jotted down over the last two quarters:
raw_unfiltered_snippets: [Exit note — Milan C++ Dev, left at month 5]: 'Job ad promised hybrid Cloud/AI R&D. Day one was 100% in-office maintaining undocumented 2014 machine-vision code. Team lead cancelled four 1-on-1s in a row.'
[Declined offer — Automation Engineer]: 'Took 26 days after the HR call just to schedule the technical talk. In the meantime I read recent Indeed software reviews and accepted another offer.'
[Plant suggestion box — Modena Assembly]: 'Coffee vending machine in Hall 2 swallows coins and visitor parking is always full on Tuesdays.'

[Exit note — Junior IoT Engineer, Milan, left at month 4]: 'Good salary and solid company, zero complaints on pay. Left because nobody explained what is expected to move from junior to mid-level and every architecture idea gets shut down.'

[Informal check-in — Senior Mechatronic Technician, 7 yrs tenure, Reggio Emilia]: 'Paycheck on the 27th never missed a beat in 7 years, €2,400 production bonus + paid overtime are better than anyone in the district—just tell recruitment ads to say what machines we actually build instead of generic slogans.'

[Informal check-in — Travelling Commissioning Tech, 2 yrs tenure]: 'Per-diem travel pay is fair, but learning on Friday at 17:30 that Monday's installation moved from Lyon to Stuttgart wrecks family weekends.'
[Plant suggestion box — Reggio Emilia]: 'Summer air conditioning in the mezzanine office takes 30 minutes to cool down after lunch.'

recent_quarter_raw_anomaly.scraper_flag: Includes 5 near-identical 5.0-star 1-line reviews submitted within 36 hours in Nov 2025 praising 'world-leading Export vision'

sample_raw_review_excerpts.text: Solid company, punctual pay, €2,400 production bonus paid every year and good canteen. Old-school hierarchy in some offices.
Recruiting ad talked about Cloud, AI and flexible work. Actual job is 5 days/week at the desk patching legacy C++ without documentation or mentoring.
Waited 2 hours in my truck under the sun at Gate B just to unload two pallets of steel frames. Warehouse office doesn't answer the intercom!
World leader in industrial excellence, proud of our 40-year history and visionary leadership!
Good base salary, but zero career ladder and newly promoted leads treat questions as an annoyance. Three colleagues in my squad left inside 6 months.
High-end machinery you can be proud to install, great overtime and travel allowances, though Friday afternoon schedule changes are stressful.

traffic_and_funnel_metrics.tracking_diagnostic_note: 'Apply' CTA opens an uninstrumented webform forwarding PDF attachments to hr-cv@... with zero pre-screening filter Questions and no conversion pixel.

career_website_and_jd_telemetry.sample_live_job_ad_text: SOFTWARE & AUTOMATION ENGINEER — Leading global industrial group seeks a dynamic, proactive resource passionate about Industry 5.0, Cloud, and AI innovation to insert into a young and stimulating environment. Flexibility, problem-solving attitude, and team spirit required. Compensation commensurate with experience.

linkedin_and_content_telemetry.format_note: 34 of 36 posts in the last two quarters were trade-fair booth photos or corporate announcements; the only 2 posts showing engineers testing a high-speed robotic line achieved 14.6% ER, then no similar posts were published for 5 months.
